title: Prediction
description: Predict why hooks must follow stable call order.
prompt: Why should hooks be called at the top level of a component?

options.label: Mostly for performance, so React can skip unnecessary work.
Because TypeScript cannot type hooks inside conditions.
So React sees hook calls in the same order every render and connects the right state to the right slot.

responses.performance-only: Not quite. Stable hook order is about correctness first. Performance is not the main reason.
responses.stable-order: Correct. React relies on hook call order to associate state and effects with a component instance.
responses.typescript-rule: Not quite. This is a React rendering rule, not a TypeScript limitation.

metadata.reason: Catches the common misconception that hook rules are arbitrary style rules.
